episodes.214774: The synoptic pattern shifted by mid July sufficiently to allow a more marked influx of monsoonal moisture into Utah. In addition to some isolated thunderstorm wind gusts, this resulted in numerous instances of flash flooding and debris flows.

episodes.215250: An upper level shortwave and surface cold front moved across a moderately unstable airmass across Ontario province and northern NY during the late evening/overnight hours of July 14th-15th.||Numerous thunderstorms entered northern NY from Ontario province with several of them producing severe weather in terms of damaging winds and large hail in St. Lawrence county.
episodes.215251: An upper level shortwave and surface cold front moved across a moderately unstable airmass across Ontario province and northern NY during the late evening/overnight hours of July 14th-15th and then moved across VT.||Numerous thunderstorms entered central and southern VT from NY state with several of them producing significant severe weather in terms of damaging winds in Addison, Rutland and Windsor counties.||Earlier in the day, a renegade thunderstorm from Quebec moved across northeast VT and produced localized minor wind damage.
episodes.215718: A strong upper-level ridge moved over the northern Great Plains allowing a moist, tropical airmass to move over South-Central Texas. Precipitable water values increased to greater than 2.0 inches which were near or above the 95th percentile of climatological values for this part of July. Multiple rounds of excessive rainfall were triggered by mid-level disturbances around the southern periphery of the high and low-level outflow boundaries. This convection was aided by nocturnal low-level jet streaks which led to slow moving, back building thunderstorms. Most of South-Central Texas received more than two inches of rain. The greatest totals were over Uvalde and Kinney Counties where 20-30 inches occurred. Another local maximum of 15-20 inches was observed in central Kerr County. Ten to 15 inches were widespread from Del Rio to Hondo and northward to northeastern Edwards to western Gillespie Counties. Damage estimates were near $115 million across South-Central Texas.
episodes.216169: A hot and unstable air mass produced isolated severe thunderstorms across Shiawassee and Oakland Counties during the afternoon of July 15th.
episodes.216338: A few thunderstorms developed along the Canadian Border during the overnight hours along a mid-level frontal boundary. There was one report of golf ball sized hail in Bottineau County, near the city of Bottineau.
episodes.216377: A cold front and upper level disturbance crossed northern Maine during the early morning hours of the 15th. Showers and thunderstorms accompanied these features. An isolated thunderstorm reached severe levels and produced localized damaging wind gusts in the Caribou area. Estimated wind gusts up to around 60 mph toppled several trees around Caribou.
episodes.216504: Deep monsoonal moisture spread over Wyoming and brought some drenching and slow moving showers and thunderstorms. To the southwest of Cody, heavy rain brought a flash flood and mudslide that severely damaged a bridge along Hunter Creek Road along the South Fork of the Shoshoni River over Boulder Creek.
episodes.216519: An upper-level disturbance and increasing monsoonal moisture brought scattered showers and thunderstorms to the region. The convective environment was favorable to produce severe thunderstorms with large hail greater than 2 and isolated flash flooding.
episodes.216670: The passage of a cold front through an abnormally warm, humid environment was sufficient to drive the development of showers and thunderstorms, largely to the north of eastern New York, in the preliminary hours of July 15th. That said, a couple of storms tracked into the Adirondacks and Upper Hudson Valley with one reaching severe strength and causing wind damage in Warren County. Just before 3 AM, a tree and wires were reported to have been downed on Schroon River Road to the southeast of Chestertown.
episodes.216671: The passage of a cold front through an abnormally warm, humid environment was sufficient to drive the development of showers and thunderstorms, largely to the north of southern Vermont, in the preliminary hours of July 15th. That said, a couple of storms tracked into Bennington and Windham County with one reaching severe strength and causing wind damage near Bellows Falls in Windham County. Just before 5 AM, trees were reportedly downed along I-91.
episodes.216802: A strong monsoon surge brought heavy rain and flooding to Northwest Arizona.
episodes.216844: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the east central Florida coast.
episodes.216971: Isolated thunderstorms produced localized wind damage on July 15.
episodes.217163: A slow moving front meandered over the region July 15 and 16 resulting in scattered storms that produced damaging winds, particularly over southeastern PA and South Jersey.
episodes.217261: Isolated, windy thunderstorms produced gusts up to 74 mph across Golden Valley and Musselshell counties.
episodes.217263: Thunderstorms impacted south-central MT, producing gusts up to 65 mph and localized rain amounts up to 3 inches within a couple hours.
episodes.217295: Continuing an active monsoon period with multiple recorded wind gusts of 51 to 68 mph in Pima, Santa Cruz, and Graham counties. Additionally, the heavy rainfall caused running washes that led to a washed out roadway with rocks and boulders in Rio Rico.
episodes.217327: Severe weather across New Hampshire on July 14-15th, 2026, was driven by an unusually potent, high-end severe setup, that was tampered by cloud cover and thick wildfire smoke from Canada.  An intense mid-level shortwave trough and an accompanying surface cold front pushed east-southeastward from Quebec and northern New York into New England. Strong wind shear (40���50+ kt deep-layer shear) paired with high storm-relative helicity supported organized supercells and embedded bowing segments.  The cloud cover and thick smoke inhibited development early in the day, but organized convection developed during the evening across Central and Northern New Hampshire and continued through the night into the early morning hours of July 15th.

Major flooding occurred along the Nueces and Frio Rivers as a flood wave moved downstream following heavy rains over the southern Edwards Plateau. The Frio River near Derby was at Major flood stage between July 17 and July 19. ||Frio County did not experience significant damage, and no homes were affected by floodwaters. However, several highways were closed due to inundation as early as July 15, including US57, Highway 85, and several other county roads and farm-to-market highways. A water rescue involving a stranded tractor-trailer occurred on July 18 on FM117. Another water rescue involving stranded kayakers on the Leona River resulted in a water rescue near CR4440 and FM1581.

Security camera footage, pictures, and radar data indicate a brief EF-0 tornado occurred just northeast of downtown San Antonio, near the Dignowity Hill district. The weak tornado traveled from near the intersection of Burleson St. and N. Olive St., |northwest to near the intersection of Milam and N. Mesquite St. More notable damage included a tin roof to a business partially peeled up as well as a brick facade partially |collapsed. Maximum winds were estimated to be 65 mph.

After receiving 2-6 inches of rain on the 14th, the Boerne area had another 6-10 inches early on the 15th. This led to severe flooding in Boerne. Water rescues were reported, and neighborhoods were cut off by flooded roads. Boerne police responded to 109 calls for service, of which 36 were high-water calls including a boat rescue of a stranded SUV at Herff Rd. and River Rd. Swift-water rescue teams extracted three people trapped in vehicles, including two walkout rescues and one boat rescue. Two of the rescues occurred at the Herff Rd. and River Rd. intersection. Most calls for service were along River Rd. and Cibolo Creek, with a few in the I-10 corridor. The city of Boerne encouraged voluntary evacuations in the Lake Country, Shoreline Park, Heart of Boerne, Evergreen, Yoalana, and West San Antonio Avenue areas. Evacuations occurred in low-lying areas near Cibolo Creek, at homes and at an apartment complex. Evacuations were also carried out along Ranger Creek and near Boerne City Lake. One home in Ranger Creek was flooded with 3 feet of water. The rise on Cibolo Creek inundated the Main St. bridge and Herff Rd. intersections and flooded River Road Park. The Herff and River Rd. intersection was under 2-3 feet of water. River Road was closed in all directions. Damage to roads and bridges around the county was estimated at $3 million.

A National Weather Service team surveyed tornado damage in northwest San Antonio. The survey team found evidence of EF-1 damage with peak winds estimated at 100 mph. The tornado began roughly two miles southwest of the I-10 and Loop 1604 interchange, near Capeswood St. where tree damage was observed, including a large tree uprooted. The tornado continued north, crossing De Zavala Rd. and W. Hausman Rd., producing damage to trees. The tornado struck an apartment complex at UTSA Blvd. and Utex Blvd., producing EF-1 damage. The south facing roof to one of the apartment buildings was removed. The tornado continued north-northeast, crossing Loop 1604. Significant tree damage was observed in the Leon Creek Greenway and along Via La Cantera. The tornado then crossed I-10 and moved into the The Rim|shopping center. Several businesses sustained roof damage in addition to glass windows being blown out. The tornado weakened and dissipated just north of The Rim.
